title: Yes! Since God Himself Has Said It
description: Yes! Since God Himself Has Said It in Tonic Solfa to KALMAR, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 52, “Confidence”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked 8.7.8.7.7.7, to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to KALMAR; any other 8.7.8.7.7.7 tune fits them as well.
underlay: Yes! since God him-self has said it, On the pro-mise I re-ly; His good word de-mands my cred-it, What can un-be-lief re-ply? He is strong and can ful-fill, He is truth and there-fore will.

lines: Yes! since God himself has said it,
On the promise I rely;
His good word demands my credit,
What can unbelief reply?
He is strong and can fulfill,
He is truth and therefore will.
As to all the doubts and questions,
Which my spirit often grieve,
These are Satan's sly suggestions,
And I need no answer give;
He would fain destroy my hope,
But the promise bears it up.
Sure the Lord thus far has brought me
By his watchful tender care;
Sure 'tis he himself has taught me
How to seek his face by prayer:
After so much mercy past,
Will he give me up at last?
True, I've been a foolish creature;
And have sinned against his grace;
But forgiveness is his nature,
Though he justly hides his face:
Ere he called me well he knew,
What a heart like mine would do.
In my Savior's intercession
Therefore I will still confide;
Lord accept my free contrition,
I have sinned, but thou hast died:
This is all I have to plead,
This is all the plea I need.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to KALMAR by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
